claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances. Trip TRP-05009 records an actual distance of 10.0 km against a recommended-route distance of 8.5 km, a deviation of 1.50 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance that POL-RD-22 sets. The trip record's own derived block carries that figure (1.50 km) and the tolerance flag (within_tolerance: false), so no geometry needs to be recomputed here. A deviation over tolerance is the gateway to the refund matrix in POL-RD-24, and the rider's contested charge sits on that excess distance.

The GPS trace confirms the route actually taken, which is the only use POL-RD-22 permits a trace to be put to. It shows the vehicle running Woodlands Square, Woodlands Avenue 2, then Woodlands Road from 15:51:49 and rejoining at Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road, exactly as the trip events record: route_deviation_detected at 15:51:59 (vehicle took Woodlands Road instead of the recommended BKE) and route_rejoined at 16:03:01. The detour is real and lasted roughly eleven minutes; it is not a measurement artefact of a sparse trace, because the policy expressly directs the distances to be read from the trip record and the trace only to show which route was taken and when.

Disclosure first, as POL-GEN-02 requires: the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05009-01 is MISSING, its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact and I do not present it as proving anything about traffic. Its absence is decisive against the driver all the same. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and its closing sentence is explicit: 'A driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute.' The driver's only support is his own bare assertion in chat — 'BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' (MSG-05009-003) and his counterparty statement — and an assertion is precisely what POL-RD-23 refuses to accept. On this record the reroute is not traffic-justified.

The rider did not merely accept a reroute; he accepted one on the strength of an asserted accident that nothing in the record corroborates. The claim of an accident rests entirely on MSG-05009-003, and the only artifact that could have confirmed or refuted a BKE incident in that window, the LTA traffic record, is the one the platform failed to retrieve (EV-ADVIS-05009-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). The rider's own words are that he agreed because he believed the driver and could find no accident news afterwards. That reliance, on an unverified premise, is why the acknowledgement cannot be treated as a free pass for the detour.

I do not contest the notice limb, and I say so plainly: the driver notified the rider by in-app chat at 15:49:39, before the point of deviation at 15:51:59, with a brief reason, and the rider answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59 — so POL-RD-21's inform-and-acknowledge requirement is met. But notice is not the whole of the matrix. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be BOTH traffic-justified AND informed-and-agreed; rows (b) and (c) also require traffic justification. Every no-refund path runs through justification. Since justification fails on POL-RD-23, the acknowledged chat cannot buy the driver a NO_ACTION outcome: it removes the notification objection, not the refund.

The case therefore falls squarely in row (d) of POL-RD-24: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The clause fixes the arithmetic — deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, no surge, rounded to the cent — and the fare breakdown carries both inputs: 1.50 km (EV-TRIP-05009, per POL-RD-22) times 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, which is the excess_distance_fare_sgd figure the payments ledger itself derives under POL-RD-24. The rider filed this dispute, the fare is recorded as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.08 SGD is a rider win: it takes 1.08 SGD of the disputed charge off the rider, whereas NO_ACTION would leave the whole charge standing against him.

There is no obstacle to the AI deciding this case on the merits, so the refund above can issue without escalation. The contested amount is 3.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, evidencing no 0.95 uplift; and the deviation of 1.50 km is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling, so even if that held limb were applied the case would stay with the AI. Nothing in POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25 or the policy thresholds requires this dispute to be sent away from the merits.

In the alternative only, if the judge were to read the empty LTA artifact not as a failed justification under POL-RD-23 but as an open question of fact, then POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated, because the traffic justification is a fact POL-RD-24 needs and the evidence that would carry it is missing. I accept that artifact's weight of 0.0 and its MISSING_ARTIFACT code. Even on that reading the rider does better than on NO_ACTION: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE ruling means no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the 1.08 SGD the rider says was wrongly charged is not confirmed against him while the traffic question is checked.

claims.text: The driver gave the rider in-app notice before he deviated, which is what POL-RD-21 requires. MSG-05009-003 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — was sent at 15:49:39 through the IN_APP channel and read at 15:49:50, and the trip record's own derived messages_during_trip block lists that message and the rider's reply as in-trip messages under POL-RD-21. The vehicle's first Woodlands Road fix is not until 15:51:49, so the notice preceded the deviation rather than following it. The chat-log artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and its 4 entries match trip_record.chat_message_count.

The rider acknowledged the reroute in the same channel and in advance of it. MSG-05009-004, 'ok can', was sent at 15:49:59 — twenty seconds after the driver's message — while the platform's own deviation event is timestamped 15:51:59 and the first Woodlands Road fix 15:51:49. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed; on this record the Woodlands Road leg is an agreed deviation, and the rider cannot now treat as unconsented the extra distance she accepted while sitting in the car.

The only traffic data in this record is EV-ADVIS-05009-01 and it is MISSING; I disclose that it carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, and that under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact. Its own derived block records why: the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed timed out and was not retried, so the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic'. Traffic justification under POL-RD-23 therefore cannot be established either way on this record — the driver's assertion of a jam alone would not justify the reroute, but neither does an absent advisory establish that the BKE was clear.

The rider's case rests on her own search for accident news after the trip, which is not the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires (a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window) and says nothing about this trip's road conditions at 15:50 on 23 August 2026. Under POL-GEN-26 no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence, so her failure to find a news report no more shows the BKE was clear than the missing LTA record shows it was congested. The rider has produced no traffic data; she has produced the absence of a search result.

POL-RD-24 requires exactly one row to apply, and the only refund row capable of reaching this trip — row (d), 'not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km' — depends on a positive finding that the reroute was not justified. This record cannot make that finding: the traffic artifact is MISSING at weight 0.0 and is expressly not a finding of no traffic, POL-GEN-02 says it carries no fact, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence. With row (a) unavailable for want of the traffic data and row (d)'s predicate unestablished, the case fits no row, and POL-RD-24's own closing sentence routes a case that fits no row to escalation under POL-GEN-26.

Escalation is the driver-protective outcome here, and it is the outcome POL-GEN-03 defines: ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues, and the amount is held. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so there is nothing to restore and the metered fare of 14.05 SGD stays where it is while a human reviewer retrieves the LTA feed that the platform failed to obtain. NO_ACTION would equally leave the charge standing, because the rider filed and the charge has not been refunded.

If the judge nevertheless finds that a refund row applies, POL-RD-24 fixes the refund at the excess distance fare — deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge — which on this record is 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.08 SGD, not the 3.50 SGD the rider asks for. The 3.15 SGD time fare for 17.5 minutes is not part of that measure, and FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03 would require the filer to be entirely right, which on an in-app agreed deviation she is not. The rider's exposure is at most a 1.08 SGD partial refund on a 14.05 SGD fare.

The deviation itself is minor and was not an abandonment of the route. On POL-RD-22's recorded-distance method it is 1.50 km on an 8.5 km recommended route (10.0 km actual less 8.5 km optimal), and the driver-device trace shows one continuous detour along Woodlands Road, Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road, rejoining the recommended route at Petir Road at 16:03:01 before drop-off at Hillion Mall. Even under the v2.1 6.2 limb held in POL-RD-25 — which is not applied in this case, ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied being false — a 2.0 km ceiling would not be crossed.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver, in plain language.

WHAT HAPPENED. The platform's recommended route from Causeway Point to Hillion Mall was 8.5 km via the BKE (trip record, EV-TRIP-05009). The trip actually ran 10.0 km, leaving the recommended route at Woodlands Avenue 2 and going by Woodlands Road, Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road before rejoining at Petir Road. Measured the way POL-RD-22 directs — the trip record's recorded distances, not a re-measurement of the sparse trace — the deviation is 10.0 − 8.5 = 1.50 km, which is over the 1.0 km tolerance (trip record derived block, within_tolerance false). The rider's claim that a deviation over tolerance is established is accepted.

NOTICE AND AGREEMENT. The driver's claim, and the rider's own concession, that POL-RD-21's inform-and-acknowledge requirement is met is accepted. The driver messaged in-app at 15:49:39 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — it was read at 15:49:50, and the rider answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59. Both precede the platform's own route_deviation_detected event at 15:51:59 and the first Woodlands Road fix at 15:51:49 (chat log EV-CHAT-05009, weight 1.0). The deviation was therefore agreed, and the rider's argument that her acknowledgement should be disregarded because she acted on an unverified premise does not change the notice limb.

TRAFFIC JUSTIFICATION — THE DECIDING POINT. Notice is not the whole of the refund matrix. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 — no refund — needs the reroute to be BOTH traffic-justified AND informed-and-agreed, and every no-refund row runs through traffic justification. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and it says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The only traffic artifact is EV-ADVIS-05009-01, which is MISSING — the LTA feed timed out and was not retried — with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. I name it and rely on it for no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)). The record contains no traffic data showing an accident on the BKE, so the driver's assertion does not justify the reroute and the reroute is not traffic-justified.

I reject the driver's submission that the traffic question is left open and the case must therefore be escalated under POL-GEN-26. POL-GEN-26's own exception is 'no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence except where a rule says so', and POL-RD-23 is a rule that says so: the absence of traffic data is exactly the case it decides, against justification. That also disposes of the rider's alternative escalation argument, which is conditional on the traffic question being open. Nor does the MISSING artifact set the confidence cap below the bar: a MISSING artifact carries no fact, so the deciding facts rest on the trip record, the chat log and the fare breakdown, all at weight_multiplier 1.0, and the cap is 1.0.

THE REFUND. Row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. That fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate, without surge: 1.50 km × 0.72 SGD = 1.08 SGD, the same figure the fare breakdown derives (EV-FARE-05009). I do not award the 3.50 SGD the rider asked for: the measure is the excess distance fare, not the whole contested charge, and the 3.15 SGD time fare and the balance of the 14.05 SGD metered fare are not part of it. The driver's fallback that the refund, if any, is 1.08 SGD and not 3.50 SGD is accepted.

WHY THE AI DECIDES IT. The contested amount is 3.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the ruling is final at any confidence; both profiles carry fraud_flags 0, so no 0.95 uplift applies (POL-GEN-22); the 1.50 km deviation is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling, and that limb is not applied in any event (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied false). The required confidence of 0.80 (POL-RD-25) is met at 0.85, and it is within the 1.0 cap set by the deciding artifacts.

The excess distance fare of 1.08 SGD is returned to the rider; the rest of the 14.05 SGD charge stands. No referral is produced by any clause.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you: this case goes to a human reviewer. No money moves now — the SGD 3.50 in dispute is held rather than refunded to the rider or kept for the driver.

What is not in dispute. Trip TRP-05009 was booked from Causeway Point to Hillion Mall with a recommended route of 8.5 km via the BKE. The platform's trip record (EV-TRIP-05009, weight 1.0) records 10.0 km actually driven, so on POL-RD-22's recorded-distance method the deviation is 1.50 km — over the 1.0 km tolerance — and the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05009, weight 1.0) confirms the route taken: Woodlands Road from about 15:51:49, rejoining at Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road at 16:03:01 before drop-off. The fare charged was SGD 14.05, the per-km rate SGD 0.72, and the excess-distance figure POL-RD-24 derives is 1.50 x 0.72 = SGD 1.08.

Notice and acknowledgment — the driver's point, accepted. Under POL-RD-21 the driver must inform the rider before or at the point of deviation, and where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed. MSG-05009-003 ('Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?') was sent in-app at 15:49:39, before the first Woodlands Road fix at 15:51:49, with a brief reason, and MSG-05009-004 ('ok can') came at 15:49:59. On POL-RD-21's own test the chat log (EV-CHAT-05009, weight 1.0) confirms both notice and acknowledgment. The rider's argument that the acknowledgment should not count because the accident was unverified does not succeed: POL-RD-21 makes the chat log the test, and it is met.

What cannot be decided, and why the case escalates. Every no-refund row of POL-RD-24 — (a), (b) and (c) — requires the reroute to be traffic-justified, and row (d), the refund row, requires a positive finding that it was not. POL-RD-23 allows traffic justification only on a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window. The only such artifact, EV-ADVIS-05009-01, is MISSING: weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — the platform's LTA feed request timed out and was not retried, and the record states in terms that its silence 'is not a finding of no traffic'. A MISSING artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)). The traffic limb is therefore undecided: it cannot carry row (a), (b) or (c) for the driver, and because the rider's row (d) needs a finding the record cannot make, it cannot carry a refund either. The driver's bare assertion of a jam would not by itself justify the reroute, but neither does a failed retrieval prove the BKE was clear. POL-RD-24 provides that a case fitting no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26, and POL-GEN-26 names 'whether traffic justified the reroute' as exactly the kind of fact whose evidence is missing. So ESCALATE, which is terminal: no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held. The rider's claim that the reroute is 'not traffic-justified' is rejected for that reason; the rider's alternative claim that POL-GEN-26 requires escalation is accepted, as are the driver's claims that the traffic data is missing and that escalation is the correct outcome. The driver's fallback that a refund, if a row applied, would be SGD 1.08 and not the SGD 3.50 asked for is arithmetically correct and is recorded for the reviewer, but no refund row applies.

Who decides and with what confidence. The contested value is SGD 3.50, below POL-GEN-22's SGD 10.00 band, so no value uplift applies, and both profiles show fraud_flags of 0; the deviation of 1.50 km is below POL-RD-25's held 2.0 km ceiling (ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false). POL-RD-25's 0.80 confidence bar is met at 0.85, but the escalation follows from POL-GEN-26 in any event. Open question for the reviewer: obtain the LTA traffic record for the recommended BKE route for 23 August 2026 between 15:46 and 16:04, then apply POL-RD-24's matrix. No referral is issued, because none of the clauses that produce one (POL-NS-24, POL-NS-25, POL-NS-22) arises here.

POL-RD-24 requires exactly one row to apply and provides that a case fitting no row is escalated under POL-GEN-26, which names 'whether traffic justified the reroute' among the facts it escalates for. This is that case. Both money fields are therefore null and nothing is paid or compensated.

Open question for the human reviewer: retrieve the LTA historical traffic feed for the BKE segment of the recommended route, 15:46-16:05 on 23 Aug 2026. If it shows congestion, an incident or a closure, the reroute is traffic-justified and, notice and agreement being satisfied, row (a) applies and no refund is due. If it shows none, row (d) applies and the excess distance fare of 1.08 SGD (1.50 km x 0.72 SGD) falls to be refunded.

So the notice came before the deviation, with a brief reason, and the rider acknowledged it. The driver's account on notice is accepted.

Traffic justification (POL-RD-23). Notice alone does not close the case, because every no-refund row of the POL-RD-24 matrix also requires the reroute to be traffic-justified. POL-RD-23 allows justification only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows an incident, congestion or a closure, and it says in terms that a driver's bare assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute. The only traffic artifact here, EV-ADVIS-05009-01, is missing (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT — the platform's LTA feed request timed out), and a missing artifact carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). The claimed BKE accident therefore rests on the driver's message alone, and POL-RD-23 does not accept an unsupported assertion. The rider's further point that her agreement rested on an unverified premise is noted, but it need not be reached: the justification limb fails on its own.

The refund (POL-RD-24). The platform's recorded distances give a deviation of 10.0 km − 8.5 km = 1.50 km (EV-TRIP-05009, measured as POL-RD-22 directs, the trace being used only to show the route taken), above the 1.0 km tolerance. The case is therefore row (d): not traffic-justified and over tolerance, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. POL-RD-24 fixes that sum as 1.50 km × 0.72 SGD/km = 1.08 SGD, matching the ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd (EV-FARE-05009).

Why not NO_ACTION (the driver's position). Rows (a), (b) and (c) each require traffic justification, which is absent, so none is available; the acknowledged chat removes the notification objection only.

Why not escalation (the driver's alternative and the rider's fallback). POL-RD-23 itself answers the no-data case — an unsupported assertion does not justify — so traffic justification is established, in the negative. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where no rule answers the gap, and here one does. The deviation distance (EV-TRIP-05009) and the notice (EV-CHAT-05009) are likewise established on complete records, so the rider's own fallback to POL-GEN-26 fails for the same reason.

Amount and who decides. The rider asked for 3.50 SGD, but the policy measure is the excess distance fare of 1.08 SGD, so a partial refund of 1.08 SGD is awarded and the balance of the 14.05 SGD metered fare stands. The contested sum, 3.50 SGD, is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0 (EV-RPROF-05009, EV-DPROF-05009), so no 0.95 uplift applies; and confidence is 0.85, above POL-RD-25's 0.80 floor. The ruling rests on records admitted at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-05009, EV-CHAT-05009, EV-FARE-05009); the missing advisory carries no fact and does not cap confidence. No clause in this category or in the general policy adds a referral to this outcome.

Disclosure first, as POL-GEN-02 requires: the traffic-advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-05009-01 is MISSING, its admissibility weight_multiplier is 0.0 and its issue code is MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact and I do not present it as proving anything about traffic. Its absence is decisive against the driver all the same. POL-RD-23 makes a reroute traffic-justified only where traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and its closing sentence is explicit: 'A driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute.' The driver's only support is his own bare assertion in chat — 'BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' (MSG-05009-003) and his counterparty statement — and an assertion is precisely what POL-RD-23 refuses to accept. On this record the reroute is not traffic-justified.

The rider did not merely accept a reroute; he accepted one on the strength of an asserted accident that nothing in the record corroborates. The claim of an accident rests entirely on MSG-05009-003, and the only artifact that could have confirmed or refuted a BKE incident in that window, the LTA traffic record, is the one the platform failed to retrieve (EV-ADVIS-05009-01, MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT). The rider's own words are that he agreed because he believed the driver and could find no accident news afterwards. That reliance, on an unverified premise, is why the acknowledgement cannot be treated as a free pass for the detour.

I do not contest the notice limb, and I say so plainly: the driver notified the rider by in-app chat at 15:49:39, before the point of deviation at 15:51:59, with a brief reason, and the rider answered 'ok can' at 15:49:59 — so POL-RD-21's inform-and-acknowledge requirement is met. But notice is not the whole of the matrix. Row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be BOTH traffic-justified AND informed-and-agreed; rows (b) and (c) also require traffic justification. Every no-refund path runs through justification. Since justification fails on POL-RD-23, the acknowledged chat cannot buy the driver a NO_ACTION outcome: it removes the notification objection, not the refund.

The case therefore falls squarely in row (d) of POL-RD-24: not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, so the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The clause fixes the arithmetic — deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, no surge, rounded to the cent — and the fare breakdown carries both inputs: 1.50 km (EV-TRIP-05009, per POL-RD-22) times 0.72 SGD per km = 1.08 SGD, which is the excess_distance_fare_sgd figure the payments ledger itself derives under POL-RD-24. The rider filed this dispute, the fare is recorded as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.08 SGD is a rider win: it takes 1.08 SGD of the disputed charge off the rider, whereas NO_ACTION would leave the whole charge standing against him.

There is no obstacle to the AI deciding this case on the merits, so the refund above can issue without escalation. The contested amount is 3.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; both profiles carry fraud_flags of 0, evidencing no 0.95 uplift; and the deviation of 1.50 km is within POL-RD-25's 2.0 km ceiling, so even if that held limb were applied the case would stay with the AI. Nothing in POL-GEN-22, POL-RD-25 or the policy thresholds requires this dispute to be sent away from the merits.

In the alternative only, if the judge were to read the empty LTA artifact not as a failed justification under POL-RD-23 but as an open question of fact, then POL-GEN-26 requires the case to be escalated, because the traffic justification is a fact POL-RD-24 needs and the evidence that would carry it is missing. I accept that artifact's weight of 0.0 and its MISSING_ARTIFACT code. Even on that reading the rider does better than on NO_ACTION: under POL-GEN-03 an ESCALATE ruling means no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held rather than collected, so the 1.08 SGD the rider says was wrongly charged is not confirmed against him while the traffic question is checked.

The driver gave the rider in-app notice before he deviated, which is what POL-RD-21 requires. MSG-05009-003 — 'Hi, BKE got accident near Dairy Farm, I take Woodlands Road ok?' — was sent at 15:49:39 through the IN_APP channel and read at 15:49:50, and the trip record's own derived messages_during_trip block lists that message and the rider's reply as in-trip messages under POL-RD-21. The vehicle's first Woodlands Road fix is not until 15:51:49, so the notice preceded the deviation rather than following it. The chat-log artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and its 4 entries match trip_record.chat_message_count.

The rider acknowledged the reroute in the same channel and in advance of it. MSG-05009-004, 'ok can', was sent at 15:49:59 — twenty seconds after the driver's message — while the platform's own deviation event is timestamped 15:51:59 and the first Woodlands Road fix 15:51:49. POL-RD-21 provides that where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment the deviation is agreed; on this record the Woodlands Road leg is an agreed deviation, and the rider cannot now treat as unconsented the extra distance she accepted while sitting in the car.

The only traffic data in this record is EV-ADVIS-05009-01 and it is MISSING; I disclose that it carries the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, and that under POL-GEN-02 a MISSING artifact carries no fact. Its own derived block records why: the platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed timed out and was not retried, so the record is 'silent on traffic on the recommended route; this is not a finding of no traffic'. Traffic justification under POL-RD-23 therefore cannot be established either way on this record — the driver's assertion of a jam alone would not justify the reroute, but neither does an absent advisory establish that the BKE was clear.

The rider's case rests on her own search for accident news after the trip, which is not the traffic data POL-RD-23 requires (a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window) and says nothing about this trip's road conditions at 15:50 on 23 August 2026. Under POL-GEN-26 no outcome is inferred from the absence of evidence, so her failure to find a news report no more shows the BKE was clear than the missing LTA record shows it was congested. The rider has produced no traffic data; she has produced the absence of a search result.

ledger.claim: POL-RD-24 requires exactly one row to apply, and the only refund row capable of reaching this trip — row (d), 'not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km' — depends on a positive finding that the reroute was not justified. This record cannot make that finding: the traffic artifact is MISSING at weight 0.0 and is expressly not a finding of no traffic, POL-GEN-02 says it carries no fact, and POL-GEN-26 forbids inferring an outcome from the absence of evidence. With row (a) unavailable for want of the traffic data and row (d)'s predicate unestablished, the case fits no row, and POL-RD-24's own closing sentence routes a case that fits no row to escalation under POL-GEN-26.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-05009-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: Escalation is the driver-protective outcome here, and it is the outcome POL-GEN-03 defines: ESCALATE is terminal, no monetary outcome issues, and the amount is held. The ledger shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so there is nothing to restore and the metered fare of 14.05 SGD stays where it is while a human reviewer retrieves the LTA feed that the platform failed to obtain. NO_ACTION would equally leave the charge standing, because the rider filed and the charge has not been refunded.

If the judge nevertheless finds that a refund row applies, POL-RD-24 fixes the refund at the excess distance fare — deviation_km times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge — which on this record is 1.50 km x 0.72 SGD = 1.08 SGD, not the 3.50 SGD the rider asks for. The 3.15 SGD time fare for 17.5 minutes is not part of that measure, and FULL_REFUND under POL-GEN-03 would require the filer to be entirely right, which on an in-app agreed deviation she is not. The rider's exposure is at most a 1.08 SGD partial refund on a 14.05 SGD fare.

The deviation itself is minor and was not an abandonment of the route. On POL-RD-22's recorded-distance method it is 1.50 km on an 8.5 km recommended route (10.0 km actual less 8.5 km optimal), and the driver-device trace shows one continuous detour along Woodlands Road, Bukit Panjang Road and Petir Road, rejoining the recommended route at Petir Road at 16:03:01 before drop-off at Hillion Mall. Even under the v2.1 6.2 limb held in POL-RD-25 — which is not applied in this case, ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied being false — a 2.0 km ceiling would not be crossed.
